newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso dips to 32-mth low on C Bank move.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso dips to 32-mth low on C Bank move.

text.p: The Philippine peso dipped to a 32-month low on Friday after the Central Bank's higher offer rate for the dollar created some panic in the market, traders said.
The peso ended at 26.39 to the dollar -- the Central Bank's new offer rate from a previous 26.375 -- and compared to Thursday's 26.372 close.
Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza said the adjustment was due to pre-weekend arbitrage plays which usually hits the peso.
"We have allowed the rate to move in accordance with what the market dictates," he said.
The rate is the lowest since October 1994, when the rate was 26.47.
Traders said the Central Bank's move pushed arbitrageurs to close their positions and buy dollars from the Central Bank.
But the Central Bank said it had also bought dollars during the day. "There must have been a big investment which came in," a trader said.
The Central Bank was estimated to have sold $129 million to $136 million at 26.39. It also bought aroun $120 million at 26.388.
Volume ballooned on Friday at $442.6 million from $203.4 million.
The peso will take its cue from any more moves by the Central Bank, traders said.
